definition: Malleable means capable of being shaped or transformed.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word malleable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know malleable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Pollsters found opinion on the new tax still malleable: one strong editorial moved the numbers eight points in a week.
Workable clay takes a thumbprint with some effort; malleable promises more — the whole form can be remade under steady pressure.
Fluid outruns malleable: a malleable thing takes a new shape and keeps it, while a fluid one holds no shape of its own at all.

Moldable is the hands-on, workshop twin: clay, dough, or warm plastic that fingers and tools can press into shape. It stays close to physical stuff you can touch. Malleable reaches further — metals, but also opinions, habits, and memories — anything outside pressure can remake into a form that then holds.

Impressionable is for minds, especially young ones: a person so easily influenced that whatever they meet leaves its mark. It rarely describes materials at all. Malleable covers both worlds — a malleable metal or a malleable opinion — and stresses that the pressure comes from outside and the new shape keeps.

Memory, they concluded, is malleable — each retelling presses it into a slightly new shape, and the new shape holds.
Malleable is the exact word because the shaping comes from outside and the result keeps: pressed once, the memory stays pressed.
Its unit-mate pliable is the springier idea — bending without breaking, and often bending back.
What is pliable yields; what is malleable is remade.
